case_studies.title: Forensic Trajectory Signatures for Agent Memory Poisoning Detection
case_studies.abstract: We discover a behavioral invariant in LLM agents under persistent memory poisoning: in architectures where routing information is retrieved through observable memory-tool invocations, successful attacks require calling memory_recall_fact before email_send_email, a transition that non-exfiltrating sessions rarely exhibit. Under the evaluated architecture, this invariant follows from the attack's information-retrieval dependency rather than being merely an empirical correlation, and suppressing it breaks the attack. A simple rule exploiting this invariant alone achieves AUC = 0.9563. A Random Fo
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of detecting memory poisoning attacks on large language models by identifying a behavioral pattern that indicates an attack is happening. The authors built a detection system that uses this pattern to flag potential attacks, resulting in a highly accurate detection rate. This is relevant to IT work as it can be used to improve security in cloud infrastructure that uses large language models.

case_studies.title: From Tool Connection to Execution Control: Benchmarking Security Invariants in MCP-Style Agent Runtimes
case_studies.abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP)-style ecosystems give language-model applications a practical connection layer for tools, resources, prompts, and transports. As agents move from connection to execution, security decisions often remain split across clients, servers, prompts, approval dialogs, OAuth deployments, and logs. case_studies.summary: This research aims to solve the problem of security decisions being split across multiple components in Model Context Protocol (MCP)-style ecosystems, the authors built a runtime that makes execution-layer invariants explicit and testable, and the result is a more secure and controlled execution environment. The research focuses on benchmarking security invariants in MCP-style agent runtimes. It has potential implications for cloud infrastructure security.

case_studies.title: Poller: Are LLMs Suitable for Evaluating the Poetry Understanding Task?
case_studies.abstract: Traditional automatic evaluation methods have been shown to be unsuitable for modern Chinese poetry because of the distinct nature of this literary genre. Human evaluation remains reliable, but is expensive and not applicable to large-scale data. In this paper, we propose Poller (Poetry LLM Evaluator), a novel method leveraging large language models (LLMs) to evaluate the poetry understanding task. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating poetry understanding with a new method called Poller, which uses large language models to mimic human evaluation, resulting in a more reliable and scalable assessment. The researchers built Poller to evaluate modern Chinese poetry, which has been challenging with traditional methods. The result shows promise for automated poetry evaluation.

case_studies.title: Safety from Honesty in a Disinterested AI Predictor
case_studies.abstract: As AI systems become more capable, training procedures that optimize for downstream outcomes risk introducing implicit agency: goal-directed behavior that designers never specified. We present a formal safety argument for the Scientist AI (SAI) Predictor, trained to approximate the Bayesian posterior conditioned on a dataset of "epistemically contextualized" natural-language statements. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of implicit agency in AI systems by introducing a formal safety argument for a disinterested AI predictor. The researchers built the Scientist AI Predictor, which honestly predicts agents, actions, and their consequences without being goal-directed. The result is a safer AI system that reduces the risk of unintended behavior.

case_studies.title: Proteus: Automated Adversarial Robustness Testing for Audio Deepfake Detectors
case_studies.abstract: We present Proteus, a framework developed at Resemble AI for automated robustness testing of our audio deepfake detection system. case_studies.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
case_studies.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) offers superior capacity transfer by supervising student-sampled trajectories with dense token-level signals. To furnish high-quality supervision sources and thereby elevate the performance frontier of distillation, an intuitive direction is to infuse privileged information to either teacher or student itself. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of on-policy distillation by introducing a new method called Dual On-policy Distillation, which aims to improve the performance of distillation by using privileged information. The researchers built a new framework that infuses privileged information into the distillation process, resulting in improved capacity transfer. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Large Language Model Agentic Workflows: A Study on N8n Ecosystem
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly being adopted in low-code and no-code automation platforms, where non-expert users design workflows that combine natural language understanding with external services and APIs. LLM agents are LLM systems that use LLMs as a core "brain" to reason, plan, and autonomously execute complex, multi-step tasks. case_studies.summary: This research studied how Large Language Models are used in low-code automation platforms, building on the n8n ecosystem to analyze over 6,000 workflows and understand their design.
